raw_recipe.headline: BBQ Dry Rub
raw_recipe.description: Try this dry rub on pork steaks and country-style ribs. My family has been making it for years.
raw_recipe.name: BBQ Dry Rub

recipeInstructions.text: Mix both sugars, salt, pepper, and paprika in a medium bowl.

review.reviewBody: Very good. I cut the whole recipe in half and added 1tblspn each of garlic powder and onion powder and just a touch of cayanne pepper. I rubbed (very liberaly!) 8 pcs of 1 1/2 inch thick chops and have enough left over for at least two more applications to chicken or ribs later! The chops got rave reviews!

Fabulous on cedar plank salmon. Rub olive oil on top and bottom of both salmon and cedar plank(soaked in water at least 2 hrs). Use dry rub both over top and under salmon. The basic flavor of the rub perfectly complements the subtle flavor imparted by the cedar. Sooo good!

Don't forget to add 2 T garlic powder, 1T onion powder. I like to dry rub them SPARINGLY the night before & store in the fridge (like a marinade, but without all the liquid). Then shortly before grilling take them out and dry rub them again.

This was great. I cut the serving size to a fourth of the original recipe, cut the salt by half and added a Tbs of garlic and onion powder per some of the other reviews. I also used smoked paprika instead of regular. I thought it was great! I used it on boneless pork chops. I let them warm up to room temperature, I slathered the rub on as thick as I could get it, waited another ten minutes and grilled them normally. My fiancée loved it! I ended up with some left overs I want to try on some country style ribs. Don't forget to pat your meat dry with paper towels before applying the rub.

I had a few leftover boneless pork chops and this looked like a great rub to try. The yield on the recipe looked like far more than I needed so I broke it down by parts so I could make as little or as much as necessary. 1 part paprika, 1 part black pepper, 2 parts salt, 5 parts brown sugar, 5 parts white sugar. I also added 1 part mesquite grill smoky rub seasoning. Took the pork chops out of the refrigerator and rubbed the mix on both sides and let it sit to come to room temperature before cooking them on the skillet. The family's response, "OMG, that's SOOO good!" Definitely making this again and will try it with other cuts of pork and other meats.

I have been on a quest for years to perfect the art of slow cooked BBQ. This is very similar to the rub i have been using for years. Just add 1/4 cup of Onion powder and you will have the Best BBQ Dry rub on the planet. Try this on Grilled pork chops and wow your guests. I Guarantee they will want the recipe before they leave. I usually marinate the pork in this rub for a min of 3 hours in the fridge. Remember to let the meat hit room temperature BEFORE you grill or BBQ.

We have used this rub on chicken for almost three years now. We first pound chicken breasts very thin, then rub them with olive oil(with minced garlic mixed into it), rub with the dry rub, let sit for a few minutes, then grill. It is AWESOME! We have served this so many times entertaining and everyone loves it! We make this monthly, except for a time when we didn't have a grill, and then we missed it alot!

I have used this several times as a dry rub on pork chops but tonight added Montreal Steak Seasoning in place of the pepper! It was even better! I used it on beef ribs generously, baked at 225 degrees for 5 hours with peach juice and water with on top of sliced onion, then put on the grill with BBQ sauce for 10 minutes. The best we'd ever had. Our guests said we should enter it in a contest for the best Beef Ribs ever!

This rub was incredible! I tweaked it a little: cut back the sugars to 1 cup each and added 2 tablespoons each of garlic powder and onion powder. Rubbed the mixture on deer steaks, wrapped them in bacon and cooked on the grill - turned out great! Plan to use on chicken, pork and beef.

Excellent rub for pork, at a fraction of the cost of what a dry rub would cost at the store. I used coarse sea salt instead of table salt, and as with any rub with high salt content, do not apply this rub any more than 15 minutes before cooking the meat. 

With this sweet rub I let the meat smoke for a couple of hours until the rub forms a crust, then use a spray bottle to spray apple juice over the meat every 30 minutes or so until it is finished cooking.

This is a great rub. I used it on both chicken and pork and it was great! I made the recipe "as-is" first and I liked it. But, I do like a little heat. So I added : 1/4 cup more brown sugar. and I added 1 Tablespoon of ground cayenne pepper & Paprika. and that did the trick... for ME. It had just a nice subtle heat to it. but not enough for the kids not to like it.

I made this for some ribs I decided to smoke and OMG amazing. But let me tell you the possibilities with this rub are endless It is also amazing on pork steak and a nice thick juicy beef steak.... Definite keeper for this house
We love this rub. It makes the tenderest pork chops on the bbq and we hardly cook pork any other way. When making for kids we cut back the pepper a little.
This rub was the best, my granddaughter loved it and she is a picky eater. Will definitely be using this recipe again
If the friends like it then it must be good. Best BBQA rub ever.
I have made this rub more times than I can count. I use it primarily on baby back ribs. Its Awesome.
Imparts a great taste to the ribs I used it on. Coupled with a generous dose of hickory in the pellet grill, all I can say is awesome!
1/4 tsp less salt than stated in recipe. Saved to my favorites!
Same here but i add cayenne cinnamon coffee garlic n chili powder
I keep a huge batch of this for a last minute dry rub for beef pork and chicken. Love it
